content.text: The governing law and venue provisions fully match our preferred position, with no arbitration anywhere in the document.

input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.
input.rationale: Section 28.1 selects the laws of the State of New York (with conflict-of-law principles disapplied and the CISG expressly excluded), and Section 28.2 confers exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York, with mutual submission to personal jurisdiction and a waiver of venue/forum objections. That is precisely the preferred position (New York law; exclusive New York County state and federal courts; courts rather than arbitration). A document-wide search for "arbitration" returned no results, so there is no arbitration seat — foreign or otherwise — and no walk-away risk of a vendor home-jurisdiction forum (Silverline Systems Ltd. is a UK entity, yet no England/Wales or other foreign venue is imposed). The carve-out in 28.2 permitting temporary injunctive relief in another competent court is mutual and preserves our ability to protect confidential information and IP quickly, so it is not adverse to us. Section 28.3's executive escalation is a fifteen-business-day good-faith meeting that expressly "does not delay urgent relief or a filing needed to preserve a limitations period," so it does not impair our access to the New York courts or emergency injunctive relief. No redline is required.
